passage:
Kemi: Ava asked again about getting a phone for her 11th birthday. She mostly wants to text her cousins.
David: If she gets a phone now, next it's social media, then she's up all night messaging strangers, and by high school her grades are in the gutter.
Kemi: I was thinking a basic one with parental controls.
cue: next it's social media, then she's up all night messaging strangers
explanation: David jumps from a basic phone to strangers and failing grades without showing why each step would follow. Parents can set limits at every stage, so the chain is far from inevitable.

whyNot.fal_appeal_to_fear: David does stir up worry, but the core move is a step-by-step chain from one phone to disaster, with no support for the links.

source: Walt Brennan, resident · Linden Park board meeting
passage: I've lived across from Linden Park for thirty years, and I love what the volunteers have done with the gardens. But this food truck proposal worries me. Today it's two trucks on Saturdays. Next year it's a dozen every day, then permanent stalls, and before long the park is just a parking lot for a strip mall.
cue: Next year it's a dozen every day, then permanent stalls
explanation: Walt leaps from two weekend trucks to a strip mall with no reason to think each step would follow. The board would have to approve every expansion, so nothing here makes the slide automatic.

whyNot.fal_false_cause: Walt isn't misreading a correlation; he strings together a series of unsupported steps that end with the park disappearing.

title: Re: Early-finish Fridays
passage: Thanks for putting the proposal together, Sam. I agree morale has been low, and I support flexibility in principle. My concern is where it leads: leave at 3 on Fridays, and soon Thursdays go the same way, then clients notice nobody picks up after lunch, and we lose the Hartley account. Can we talk Monday?
cue: soon Thursdays go the same way, then clients notice nobody picks up after lunch
explanation: Harriet grants the morale problem but then predicts a slide from Friday afternoons to losing a major client. She gives no evidence for each step, and the team could set coverage rules to stop it.

whyNot.fal_appeal_to_fear: Harriet's worry isn't just emotional pressure; she builds a chain from one early Friday to a lost account without backing any link.

passage: Our department is debating whether to allow spellcheck on in-class essays. I get the case for it, especially for students with dyslexia, and that matters. But once spellcheck is in, students stop learning to spell, then they stop proofreading altogether, and in a few years we'll have graduates who can't write a sentence without an app.
cue: students stop learning to spell, then they stop proofreading altogether
explanation: Ms. Iqbal moves from spellcheck on essays to graduates who can't write, with no evidence for each link. Students still read, write and get feedback in many other ways, so the slide isn't shown.

whyNot.fal_false_cause: She isn't inferring cause from a correlation; she predicts a run of escalating effects without showing any of them is likely.

passage:
Marco: Can my team use our own process to publish the phone app update? The shared tool can't do a step we need yet.
Liz: If we make an exception for you, every team will want one. That's how the record-keeping rules fell apart last year. Then nobody can cover another team's emergency shift, and the first big website failure takes days to fix.
cue: Then nobody can cover another team's emergency shift, and the first big website failure takes days to fix
explanation: Liz cites one past case, which makes the first step plausible, but then jumps to an outage nobody can fix. A temporary exception for a missing feature doesn't make that whole chain likely.

whyNot.fal_appeal_to_fear: Liz isn't only raising alarm; she offers a chain of steps and supports just the first, letting the rest ride on it.

title: Trustee warns fine-free plan could unravel library lending
passage: Library trustee Hal Benedetti opposed the proposal to scrap overdue fines at Tuesday's meeting. Without fines, he argued, fewer books will come back, waitlists will grow, frustrated patrons will stop visiting, and falling visits will hand the county a reason to cut the library's budget. The board votes next month.
cue: fewer books will come back, waitlists will grow, frustrated patrons will stop visiting
explanation: Benedetti strings together four steps that each sound plausible, but offers no evidence for any of them, such as return rates at libraries that dropped fines. Small doubts at each link add up.

whyNot.fal_false_cause: He isn't drawing a cause from a correlation; he predicts a cascade from one policy change without supporting the links.

title: Please don't skip this year's fire inspection
passage: I know the inspection is a hassle during audit season, but it can't slide. Our insurance policy (section 4.2) requires a current annual fire certificate, and without it the policy lapses at renewal on March 1. Our lease, clause 11, requires active coverage at all times. So skipping the inspection would put us in breach of the lease.
cue: Our insurance policy (section 4.2) requires a current annual fire certificate
explanation: Tomasz traces a chain of consequences, but each link is backed by a specific document: the policy clause, the renewal date and the lease clause. That makes his conclusion a fair warning, not a scare.

whyNot.fal_slippery_slope: Every step from skipped inspection to lease breach is tied to a written requirement, so the chain is documented rather than assumed.

source: Transit planner Ana Oyelaran · Carver city council
passage: Cutting Route 9 from every 15 minutes to every 30 will cost us riders. When Halden made the same cut in 2023, weekday ridership fell 18% within a year, and in our own survey a third of Route 9 riders said they'd switch to driving if waits doubled. Fewer riders also means a smaller state transit grant, which is paid per rider.
cue: When Halden made the same cut in 2023, weekday ridership fell 18% within a year
explanation: Ana's chain of consequences is backed at each step: a comparable city's results, local survey data and the grant formula. That makes her warning a supported prediction rather than a slide into fantasy.

whyNot.fal_slippery_slope: Each link, from fewer buses to fewer riders to a smaller grant, comes with evidence instead of being simply asserted.
